title: Settings
subtitle_directory: Directory (LDAP / Active Directory) synchronization and account mapping
subtitle_backup: Enterprise SQLite hot snapshot backup, file download, and point-in-time disaster recovery
notice_not_accounts_title: Synced people are not console accounts.
notice_not_accounts_body: They have no password and cannot log in here. Their only use is as the list a hardware asset's PIC is chosen from.
connection_hint: Use a read-only service account, never your own login.
port_hint: 636 is LDAPS; 389 with TLS on is StartTLS.
transport_hint: Plain sends the bind password in the clear. Only for a tunnel you control.
base_dn_hint: The subtree to search. Everything under it is read.
bind_password_set: Set in the LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD environment variable. It is never shown, never stored in the database, and cannot be changed from here.
bind_password_unset: Not set. Export LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD and restart the server before syncing.
sync_hint: Preview shows what would change. Nothing is written until Apply.
no_preview_yet: Run a preview to see what a sync would do. Nothing has been read from the directory yet.
preview_empty_warning: The directory answered but returned no entries. A base DN that matches nothing looks exactly like an up-to-date directory, so check the base DN and filter before trusting a zero here.
nothing_to_do: Nothing to do. {unchanged} of {total} entries already match.
apply_dialog_message: Write {added} new, {updated} updated and {deactivated} deactivated contacts? Deactivated contacts drop out of every PIC dropdown and cannot come back without another sync. The server re-reads the directory on confirm, so these numbers can shift if it changed in the meantime.
dr_notice_body: Live database hot snapshots use SQLite {vacuum} for non-blocking, defragmented snapshots. Before any restore, an automated pre-restore safety snapshot ({pattern}) is captured, and all incoming backup files are verified via {check}.
kpi_snapshots_hint: Historical files in server backup storage
upload_hint: Upload a {ext} file from another host or offline storage. Verified with quick_check prior to restore.
server_snapshots_hint: Snapshots stored in the server backup directory. Select a file to download, restore, or delete.
empty_backups: No backup files found. Click "Create Snapshot" above to take a manual hot snapshot.
restore_dialog_question: Are you sure you want to restore the database from {file}?
restore_dialog_warning: An automatic safety backup ({pattern}) will be created immediately before restore. The server service will restart to reload the new database.
upload_dialog_question: Are you sure you want to upload and restore from {file} ({size})?
upload_dialog_warning: The uploaded file will be verified using {check}. An automatic safety snapshot will be taken before the active database is replaced.
delete_dialog_message: Are you sure you want to delete "{filename}" ({size})? This cannot be undone.
restarting_hint: The database has been replaced and the server service is restarting.
restore_back_online: Server is back online with restored database.
preview_nothing_matched: The directory answered but matched nothing — check the base DN and the search filter.
sync_up_to_date: Already up to date — no changes.
restore_signin_again: Sign in again if asked: your session belonged to the database that was replaced.
restore_failed_rolled_back: The restore failed. The previous database was put back and the server restarted on it; nothing was lost.
restore_failed_rollback_failed: The restore failed and the database file could not be replaced at all (another program may be holding it). The database was left as it was; check the server log.
restore_timeout: The server did not come back within 3 minutes. Check that its service is running; the outcome is shown under Last restore once it is up.
restore_safety_snapshot_failed: The safety snapshot taken before every restore failed, so the restore was not started.
